advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Unescape the destination before stripping query/fragment (or split on unescaped `?`/`#` only) so escaped `\#`/`\?` in filenames are not truncated.
evidence: `_QUALIFIER_RE = re.compile(r"[?#]")` splits on unescaped-vs-escaped `#`/`?` identically because it runs before `_unescape_destination`, so `a\#b.md` -> path_part `a\` (trailing backslash kept), losing the intended `a#b.md`.
advisory.finding: Query/fragment stripping runs on the still-escaped raw target before backslash-unescaping, so a target whose filename contains an escaped `#` or `?` (e.g. `a\#b.md`) is truncated at the literal `#`/`?` and resolved against the wrong path, producing a spurious or wrong finding.
scenarios: A Markdown link whose destination contains a backslash-escaped `#` or `?` as part of a real filename.
advisory.suggested_fix: Apply `_unescape_destination` first, then split on `?`/`#`; or scan for the first UNescaped `?`/`#` when computing `path_part`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fail (or warn loudly) when a declared MARKDOWN_SOURCE_TREES entry or MARKDOWN_SOURCE_FILES path does not exist, so a moved/renamed documented tree cannot silently drop out of coverage.
evidence: scripts/check_docs_index.py:115: `if tree.is_dir():` (missing tree is silently skipped, no error)
scripts/check_docs_index.py:121: `if path.is_file():` (missing declared file e.g. tests/unit/fixtures/README.md silently skipped)

The declared boundary in MARKDOWN_SOURCE_TREES/MARKDOWN_SOURCE_FILES is a membership contract; a miss produces nothing, and produces nothing whether the tree is clean or was moved away — the absence of findings cannot distinguish 'scanned and clean' from 'not scanned'.
advisory.finding: Declared Markdown source trees and files are silently skipped when they do not exist (`if tree.is_dir()` / `if path.is_file()`), so if a documented tree is renamed or moved the checker stops covering it and still exits 0 — a fail-open in which 'boundary member never scanned' is indistinguishable from 'boundary member clean'.
scenarios: A documented source tree (e.g. src/rebar/_guides) or the declared tests/unit/fixtures/README.md is renamed/removed and nobody updates the boundary constant.
advisory.suggested_fix: Emit an error/non-zero when a declared source tree directory or declared source file is absent, asserting the boundary constants stay in sync with the repository layout.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with a `~~~`-delimited fenced block containing a nonexistent link target and assert find_link_findings returns no finding for it.
evidence:
ABSENCE: no test feeds a source such as `~~~
[fenced](missing.md)
~~~
`; find_link_findings would need to return [] for the tilde branch to be verified
advisory.finding: The tilde-fence masking branch of the new fence parser is untested. `_FENCE_RE` (added) accepts `~{3,}` as an alternative fence marker and `_mask_fenced_blocks` masks such blocks, but every fence test uses only backtick fences (```` ```md ````). A regression that stopped recognizing `~~~` fences would emit a spurious finding for links inside them yet pass the whole suite.
scenarios: A Markdown source uses `~~~` fenced blocks (common when the block itself contains backticks) containing an example broken link.
advisory.suggested_fix:
Add a fixture line `"~~~
[fenced](missing-tilde.md)
~~~
"` to an existing no-findings test and assert the tilde-fenced target produces no LinkFinding.
